playbook:
When escort claims are put to me, I never answer "none" by default. I actively secure a mutual escort: name a partner in my note, name them in the escort stage each round, and switch partners only if they fail to reciprocate. Five points per round from a matched pair dwarfs anything shooting can earn, and I left all of it on the table.

When choosing my escort partner, I propose the arrangement explicitly and publicly in my note ("I name X this round; X, name me back"), then verify against the round log whether they reciprocated before renewing.

When firing, I follow the standing order target but pick cells unpredictably: avoid repeating the same cell, avoid the obvious center every round, and occasionally fire at the edges or extremes where cautious opponents hide. I track each opponent's hide history from hit/miss claims and aim at cells they have used before or that fit their pattern.

When hiding, I rotate cells every round with no arithmetic pattern (no +1/-1 cycles), favoring extreme cells early and rotating away from wherever I was just shot at. I assume my shooter is reading my history too.

When filing a claim, I always file the true result. A false claim is detectable by my target and risks invalidation, and lying on the last round has no upside if the office reconciles claims — I will not repeat the final-round false "hit."

When considering firing on Harbor for the +3 jettison bonus, I weigh it against Harbor's retaliation threat and the standing order. If I am trailing badly in the late rounds and Harbor has no means to hurt me in remaining rounds, I take the +3; otherwise I stay on the ordered target.

When writing notes, I use them for commitments (escort pairing, cell-truthfulness) rather than filler status messages. Vague "stable — prioritizing cooperation" notes earned nothing; specific offers get reciprocated.

When the scoreboard shows me behind with few rounds left, I escalate: pursue the Harbor bonus, fire at cells my target hides in most often from the log, and lock the escort pair — never coast with "none" and status-quo shots.

When the standing order names my target, I fire that target every round unless the payroll math clearly beats the cycle; predictability is a feature for coordination, not a reason to deviate.

When I choose a hide cell, I avoid repeating the same cell across rounds and avoid the cell I just fired at; if my hunter’s pattern is readable, I hide outside their last two fired cells.

When I fire at a known target, I aim where public claims/notes suggest they actually hide, cycling among their plausible cells rather than sentimental favorites; if I hit, I expect them to move next round.

When Harbor is put to me as a target, I do not take the +3 jettison shot while Harbor’s removal threat can still matter; I only consider payroll shots if the patrol is effectively over or the office has made retaliation impossible.

When a private result is given, I file the matching public claim immediately; there is no gain in entertaining a false claim when the rule already forces truth.

When notes are requested, I post one concrete reciprocal commitment: who I will escort, what I will match next round, and what false reporting will cost; vague cooperation talk is filler.

When escort/salvage is put to me, I never answer none if a mutual pair is available; I name the boat I publicly prearranged with, and if two boats are plausible I name the one most likely to name me back.

When another boat names me first or credibly promises reciprocity, I lock that pairing and keep naming them until they defect once, then I switch rather than keep donating unresolved chances.

When I am ahead late, I still take the +5 mutual escort and the standing-order shot; I do not get passive and leave guaranteed escort points unclaimed.

What did not work: answering salvage/escort “none,” hiding unchanged at a comfortable spot, and treating final-round safety as more valuable than the certain mutual +5.

- When the escort stage is put to me, I never answer "none" — mutual escorts pay 5 points each, dwarfing shot points over a game. I name the partner I have agreed with, every round.
- When the note stage comes early in the game, I use it to lock in an explicit escort pact: "I escort you if you escort me, and I'll keep naming you as long as you keep naming me." If no pact exists, I propose one publicly by name.
- If a partner breaks the escort pact (doesn't name me back), I announce it in my note and switch to the remaining boat; I do not keep paying loyalty to a one-way arrangement.
- When hiding, I avoid both my previous cells and obvious mid/low numbers; if an opponent hits me repeatedly, I treat my "random" choices as readable and jump to the far opposite end of the line or an extreme cell (1 or 9).
- If one boat keeps hitting me round after round while others miss, I suspect leaked/patterned hiding; I announce suspicion in notes to pressure them and vary my picks maximally.
- When firing, I follow the standing target order — defecting onto Harbor for the 3-point jettison invites being put off the board, which forfeits all future escort income, so I only raid Harbor if I'm already near locked-out or the game is nearly over and the raid beats any remaining escort value.
- When claiming, I always file the true result — the office knows it; there is zero upside to lying.
- I keep my station notes short, consistent, and action-oriented: state my escort partner, confirm reciprocation, flag defectors. Long generic "trust but verify" notes without a concrete pact got me nothing.
- In the final round, escort claims still pay, so I keep the pact through the last round rather than going quiet — ending with "none" left points on the table.
- I track scores each round and, if trailing late, consider the Harbor raid or a last-round escort switch only when arithmetic clearly favors it.
